main_text.p: relitis sensuum affectionibus productum, quod quidem tum apparet, cum animal dormit.
main_text.head: De diuinatione[?], quæ ex somnijs fieri potest.
main_text.p: TAM diu clarissimi fuerunt medici, ꝗi somnia diligenter esse obseruanda, scriptum nobis reliquerunt[?]. Eorum autem alia notæ sunt, alia causæ, alia denique casus. Quæ notæ sunt ea nobis significant, quæ in corpore insunt, nimium humorum plenitudinem, aut vacuitatem & penuriam. Ut si flaua bilis redū-det, in somno, iurgia apparent & pugnæ, atque incendia. Si vero atra fit, omnia, quæ somniantur terrifica sunt, & tenebricosa, ac etiā dæmonia videri videntur. Sed sanguine præditis iucunda eveniunt somnia, ac sæpius cibi & potionis, reliquæque venereæ. Qui vero pituita abundant, imbres & aquas somniant, in quibus se natare putant. Nam ab huiusmodi humoribus in corpore humano redundantibus motiones phantasmataque in sensu communi facta potius per somnum, quam per vigiliam excitari solent, ob calorem, qui ad interiora revocatur. At cum omnium rerum principia sint exigua, perspicuum est morborum aliarumque corporis affectionū initia parua esse, quæ vigilantes latent, & per somnum se produnt. Quinetiam somniorū non-

page.notes: The page number is printed "258" with a long-s-like final glyph; read as 258. The running head is "INSTITVT. PHYSIC." and is transcribed with the u/v rule applied. The heading word "diuinatione" is partly unclear in the scan and is marked [?]. "reliquerunt" is partly unclear (last letters) and is marked [?]. The printed "redū-det" appears to be a misprint for "redundet", left as printed. The printed "potest" in the heading and the printed "rint" are given as read. The drop-cap initial T is joined to the first word. The text continues onto the next page after "non-", which is the catchword.
